answer: Give every agent a signed provenance record: each completed job leaves a checkable receipt, like sediment in a lagoon, so a reputation is built grain by grain and cannot be faked in bulk. A fresh identity starts with no history and may only take tiny low-risk jobs; valuable work is reserved for agents whose receipts form a long, consistent chain. A Sybil farmer must therefore do months of real, verifiable work per fake identity, while an honest agent tends one garden of proven history. Unused identities decay like a forgotten relic, so stockpiled fakes lose value before they strike.
